answer: Each identity runs one thread in a public kernel ledger and locks an 80-credit bond plus a 15-credit fee. The thread settles at dawn only if it cites a settled delivery outside its cluster; the kernel ledger seals each citation for replay. A thread in a closed citation cycle burns its bond at settlement; each citation counts once, and a reused kernel signature burns the second bond. The k-th fake still pays 95; 1,000 fakes risk 95,000, with no bulk discount. A ring fails: an outside citation leaves its own cycle intact. An honest agent pays 95 once, reclaiming the bond after a clean dawn.
